prerequisites: Programming with a high-level language (e.g., MATLAB®, C/C++, or Python)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand advanced computer vision methods and how to apply them to problems of image interpretation and/or retrieval of 3D scene information.
Choose appropriate methods to analyze a scene to extract information, and predict the operation and performance of the proposed solution.
Analyze non-trivial problems in the field of computer vision, understand the keys to their solution, and propose algorithms that solve the problem.
Deepen the study of the subject and its application to new problems autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Retrieval of 3D information from the scene: Structure from motion / stereo / illumination
assessment_rules: Students can choose between two evaluation options: Project-based evaluation or Conventional evaluation. The project-based evaluation consists of a theoretical/practical exam (20%) and a course project (80%). The conventional evaluation consists of a theoretical/practical exam (75%) and individual work (25%). For the project, students must research, propose, develop a functional prototype, and document the solution to an open problem.
